act: Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (Union law — Sch. I Art. 62(a), pre-amendment)

source.ref: Indian Stamp Act, 1899, Sch. I Art. 62(a) + S.O. 130(E) dated 28-1-2004 (corrected by S.O. 522(E) dated 7-4-2005)
source.quoted_text: Central Sch. I Art. 62: 'TRANSFER (whether with or without consideration) — (a) of shares in an incorporated company or other body corporate — [Twenty-five paise] for hundred rupees or part thereof of the value of the share' = 0.25%, with the 2004 order's 'rounded off to the next five paise' proviso. NOTE: transfer of SHARES is Union law — the Karnataka Schedule Art 52 'Transfer' has NO shares clause (it covers only debentures, interest secured by a bond/mortgage-deed/policy, Administrator-General property, and trust property), so the Union Art 62(a) applies directly. Governs transfers executed BEFORE 1 July 2020.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Historical version for Flow D. effective_from is the KA 2016-04-01 coverage floor (see KA back-catalogue note), not a rate-change date — the 0.25% central rate ran from 1-3-2004.

source.ref: Finance Act 2019 (Part I, Ch. IV) amendments to the Indian Stamp Act + MoF notifications dated 10-12-2019 and 30-03-2020 (regime effective 1-7-2020)
source.quoted_text: Founder ruling (Q4, 2026-07-16): physical share transfers (Form SH-4) attract 0.015% of consideration under the amended Art 62, uniform across India from 1 July 2020; no state deviation is permitted. Gifts (nil consideration) attract nil duty per the DEA FAQs. Corroborated structurally: the Karnataka Schedule Art 52 has no competing share-transfer entry.
